notes: PARENTAGE LIKELY A DUPLICATE-RECORD CONFLATION (research 2026-07-03): this John Murray (b. 1 Feb 1677, Ewes, Dumfries; d. 27 Feb 1728) is very likely being conflated with a different, well-documented person of IDENTICAL birth and death dates and a similar name/place tag: 'John Murray of Unthank' (b. 1 Feb 1677, Unthank, Ewes, Dumfriesshire - d. 27 Feb 1728, Ancrum, Roxburghshire; WikiTree Murray-5878; Geni). That documented person's father was John Murray of Bowhill, Selkirkshire (not 'Sir James Murray of Philiphaugh,' this record's listed parent, I182381538436), his great-grandfather was James Murray of Philipaugh (d. bef. 1648) — two generations further back — and his wife was Anne Bennet (m. 1712, Ancrum), not Isobel Grant; his children were James, John, and Elizabeth (m. Inman), not William. The 'Philiphaugh' parentage in this tree appears to be a mis-transcription of this unrelated gentry line's great-grandfather onto the Eskdale farming family that is the actual ancestor, likely because a family-history compiler matched the two 'John Murray, 1677-1728' records by date alone. Per WikiTree Murray-2863, this Eskdale John Murray's real documented parentage is simply unknown; treat 'Sir James Murray Philiphaugh' as legend, unsupported for this line.
